questions.q: Every autonomous database pipeline in the chapter follows which fundamental shape?
options: plan → build → test → deploy → monitor
ingest → transform → load → validate → report
collect → correlate → classify → decide → act → audit
observe → alert → ticket → fix → close
questions.explain: The chapter states every autonomous database pipeline follows: collect → correlate → classify → decide → act → audit, with closed-loop feedback at every stage.

questions.q: What are the bounded end-to-end latency targets from signal detection to action execution?
options: Under 90 seconds for P1-class events, under 10 minutes for P2-class events
Under 1 second for all events
Under 24 hours for P1, under 7 days for P2
There are no latency bounds — each stage runs independently
questions.explain: The key architectural property is asynchrony with bounded latency: under 90 seconds for P1-class events and under 10 minutes for P2-class.

questions.q: The deterministic rule overlay in the anomaly scorer forces confidence to 0.95 when:
options: The Kafka consumer lag exceeds 288 messages
z_score_exec > 4.5, miss_ratio > 0.85, or avg_temp_blks > 5000
The IsolationForest model file is older than 24 hours
Fewer than 10 samples exist in the rolling window
questions.explain: The rule overlay sets rule_triggered when z_score_exec > 4.5 or miss_ratio > 0.85 or avg_temp_blks > 5000, raising final confidence to 0.95.

questions.q: Which action is inside the chapter's safe action envelope for autonomous execution?
options: Schema changes on any table
ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET MAXDOP, bounded to values 1–8
KILL on sessions belonging to known application service accounts
Index creation on tables larger than 10 GB outside a maintenance window
questions.explain: The safe envelope includes ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET MAXDOP bounded to [1, 8]; the other options are explicitly listed as outside the envelope.

questions.q: Before the action executor touches production, its pre-flight check includes:
options: Re-querying to confirm the condition still exists, checking no conflicting action is in progress via a distributed lock, a circuit breaker that halts if more than 3 autonomous actions ran on the host in the last 15 minutes, and confirming no maintenance suppression flag is active
Asking a human to approve every action over Slack
Waiting 24 hours and re-running the anomaly detector
Taking a full database backup before each action
questions.explain: The chapter's four pre-flight checks are: re-verify the condition, distributed lock for conflicting actions, circuit breaker at 3 actions per 15 minutes, and maintenance suppression flag.
